newsitem.title: UK: Channel tunnel repairs will take three months.
newsitem.headline: Channel tunnel repairs will take three months.

text.p: Tunnel repairs on the Channel Tunnel after a truck transporter train fire will take at least three months, its operators Eurotunnel said on Sunday.
The heat from last Monday's fire was so intense that some concrete segments of the tunnel may have to be removed and new ones installed.
"It will be at least three months," Eurotunnel's director of public affairs John Noulton told the Independent on Sunday.
"That estimate includes clearing away the remains of the shuttle train, replacing fixed equipment and replacing and repairing part of the tunnel," he told the newspaper.
The tunnel reopened for limited business on Thursday.

The Anglo-French safety commission cleared freight trains to move through the undamaged portion of the France-to-Britain tunnel, then to transfer through a junction point to the Britain-to-France tunnel which was entirely clear for operations.
The fire on a truck-carrying shuttle train had resulted in all traffic being suspended. It unleashed a storm of criticism of the tunnel's much-vaunted safety systems.
The leader of the British firefighters' union has accused the commission of complacency and called for the tunnel to remain closed until safety improvements were made.

"There should now be an urgent public inquiry into the fire and until such an inquiry can guarantee that safety is adequate, no one should go through the tunnel," said Ken Cameron, general secretary of the Fire Brigades' Union.
